articles.titre: Poland's Tusk: It doesn't look probable that Russia will be ready to negotiate peace before spring
articles.resume: Poland's Tusk has evidently heard something that's dimmed his hopes for real peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. He said that it doesn't look probable that Russia will be ready to negotiate on Ukraine before the end of winter. At the same time, Ukraine's governement bonds have had their biggest fall in a month today. That's a clear indication that the market sees a dimmed chance of peace. It comes after the Putin, Xi and Trump meeting in China this week, where peace was surely discussed. articles.titre: Moody’s keeps US rating at Aa1 as the economy beats forecasts, seeing 2.3% growth this year
articles.resume: A stable Aa1 outlook removes one source of headline risk for Treasuries, but the growth upgrade cuts the other way for bonds. Stronger-than-expected activity strengthens the hawkish case being made by Fed officials this week and supports pricing for a December hike, which should keep front-end yields and the dollar firm. That’s a headwind for gold, which has tended to fall as Fed hike expectations build. Moody’s flagged energy prices as a drag on growth, a reminder that oil is the swing factor: further strength in crude would hurt growth and keep inflation pressure alive at the same time. -- Moody’s says the US economy has outperformed, and it’s leaving the rating alone.
